step: melt with water and salts, spray-dry
text: Cheese is minced, melted with water and emulsifying salts (usually phosphates) into a uniform "cheese feed", heated, often homogenised, and sprayed into hot air. Without the salts the hot cheese parts into fat and water, and the powder comes out coarse, dark and lumpy.

links.name: Felix da Silva et al., Powder Technology 378 (2021) 227–236

steps.name: melt
steps.note: With water and emulsifying salts, usually phosphates (about 3.5 %), into a uniform cheese feed of about 38 % dry matter.
Sprayed into hot air, 190 °C in and 60 °C out.
